exposure: Trophoblastic microcirculation occlusion (TMO) as an adjunct to electric vacuum aspiration
outcome: Reduced risk of hemorrhage during electric vacuum aspiration
Complete removal of products of conception (no uterine remnants)
Subsequent intrauterine pregnancy and live birth (in one patient)
cohort: Seven women diagnosed with endogenous cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP), including a 30-year-old woman with a 5-week CSP and 6 other patients.
finding: Trophoblastic microcirculation occlusion (TMO) treatment, when used as an adjunct before high-risk electric vacuum aspiration for endogenous cesarean scar pregnancy, was successfully performed in all 7 patients and significantly reduced the risk of intraoperative hemorrhage and complications.
mod_finding: One patient achieved an intrauterine pregnancy 7 months postoperatively and gave birth to a live baby at 39 weeks of gestation via repeat cesarean section, with no cesarean scar dehiscence observed.
followup_time: Weekly until b-hCG levels normalized and follow-up ultrasound confirmed no remnants (typically several weeks); one patient was followed for 7 months post-procedure for a subsequent pregnancy.
